_: Fault stages — this design's bosses. Three per act, offered as a choice of 3 at the act's start. See docs/06-stages-and-bosses.md. Every name is a real weaving defect.
_placement: Faults sit at stages 4, 8 and 12 — the last stage of each act. The act's three options are announced when the act begins, so the player can draft toward the one they chose.

knot._: Shared mechanic used by slubs, the_smash and floats. Defined once so the three faults behave identically.
knot.rule: A knot is a filled cell that COUNTS toward completing a row or column, but is NOT removed when that line clears.
knot._why: If knots blocked lines from clearing, a single knot would kill a row and a column outright and the fault would be a coin flip. Counting-but-persisting makes a knot a creeping tax on board space instead — obstructive, survivable, and it still rewards clearing around it.
knot.allKnotGuard: A line containing no ordinary filled cell does NOT clear and does NOT score.
knot._guardWhy: Without this, a row that has become entirely knots is permanently 'full', so it re-clears on every placement and pays the line bonus forever. Floats and The Smash can both reach that state in a long stage.

rewardTiers.2: draft offers uncommon or better only
rewardTiers.3: draft offers rares only, or take an extra pick

acts.name: Act 1 challenges
acts._: Mild and legible. Their job is to teach what a fault IS, against a target of only 1.2x floor capability.

faults.name: Columns Only
faults.rule: only columns clear this level; full rows do nothing
faults.attacks: row-focused builds and the Row Bonus upgrade

faults.name: Short Fuse
faults.attacks: fast builds that rely on setup moves

acts.name: Act 2 challenges
acts._: Real tests against 3.0x floor capability. Each invalidates one archetype's main plan.

faults.name: No Rotation
faults.rule: rotation is disabled for this level

faults.name: Big Pieces Only
faults.rule: you are only dealt pieces of 4 blocks or more
faults.attacks: small-piece builds and the Small Block Guarantee

faults.name: Blockers
faults.rule: six blockers are scattered on the board at the start
faults.attacks: builds that control which blocks they get

acts.name: Act 3 challenges
acts._: The finale, against 7.4x floor capability. Each should be survivable by at least three archetypes and trivial for none.

faults.name: Narrow Board
faults.rule: the board is 7x7 for this level; lines are 7 blocks long
faults._impl: Genuinely resize the board rather than knotting the outer ring — a ring of knots would be an all-knot line and needs the guard, and 7-long lines are the clearer read. Cells in the discarded row and column are lost, which is thematically the reed tightening and the cloth narrowing.
faults.attacks: big pieces; a squeeze on everything

faults.name: Creeping Blockers
faults.rule: every third move, a random empty cell becomes a blocker
faults.attacks: long slow levels; rewards clearing fast

faults.name: Sticky Blocks
faults.rule: any move that clears no line leaves one of its blocks behind as a blocker
faults.attacks: setup play, brutally — it demands a clear almost every turn

_ifEveryStage: If faults were ever moved to every stage rather than every fourth, this roster would need 12+ entries and the act tiers would have to become a per-stage escalation curve. docs/06 §6 argues against it: with twelve disruptions there is no baseline, nothing reads as special, and planning collapses into reacting.
